items.text: A group of Iranians living in Sweden gathered with Israelis in front of the Israeli embassy in Stockholm on Wednesday, October 7. The gathering was held in memory of the victims of the October 7 attack. Videos of the event were received by Iran International.

Hojat Karimi, CEO of Tractor, stated that Alireza Beiranvand has received 35% of his contract while other players have received about 8%. He confirmed the club's financial problems and said there is a plan to increase the payment percentage to players. Karimi also commented on Beiranvand's behavior after the match and the goal he conceded.

Alireza Namvar Haghighi stated that despite Donald Trump's mention of continuing negotiations with Tehran, it is unlikely Washington will accept the Islamic Republic's conditions. He added that mistrust between the two sides is high and an agreement is likely to be step-by-step. Additionally, developments in Yemen, sanctions, and the energy market may influence the negotiation process.

Trump stated that fake media are falsely accusing him of inviting the enemy to bomb San Diego and Los Angeles. He said he was only discussing a temporary increase in gasoline prices to prevent Iran from obtaining nuclear weapons. Trump called these accusations false and a result of fake news.

Donald Trump announced that constructive negotiations with the Islamic Republic of Iran are ongoing. He emphasized that there will be no attack on Iran before the November 3 midterm elections. He also stated that Iran will not have nuclear weapons.

Zartosht Ahmadi Ragheb, a political prisoner in Karaj Central Prison, was transferred to solitary confinement. This transfer occurred while he was on the fifth day of a hunger strike. The news was reported by HRANA news agency.

Alireza Kiani discussed the necessity of support from foreign forces aligned with Iranian national interests in episode 14 of the program "Fereydoun." This topic was raised in the context of the struggle against the Islamic Republic. He emphasized the importance of such support.

The Houthi military spokesman repeated the group's warning to Saudi Arabian airlines and airports. Oil facility workers were warned to avoid locations targeted by the Houthis. Reuters also reported smoke rising from a plane at King Khalid Airport in Riyadh.

Alireza Kiani discusses the civil rights movement in the US in episode 14 of the program 'Fereydoun'. He examines the relation of this movement to the struggle against the Islamic Republic. This topic is covered in part of the program.

Lionel Messi returned to Inter Miami training two days after retiring from the Argentina national team. He will no longer leave club training for international breaks and tournaments. Inter Miami has three important MLS matches in the next 10 days.

The Washington Post reported that the escalation of attacks by the Islamic Republic on ships in the Strait of Hormuz has disrupted commercial shipping and energy transit. According to the report, at least 9 ships have been targeted in a week. The volume of crude oil passing through has decreased and the transit of gasoline and diesel has stopped.

After the violent suppression of the national revolution in December, protests have continued in the form of tattoos on the bodies of protesters and families seeking justice. These tattoos include national symbols and images of protesters killed in December. The Islamic Republic has responded to this form of protest with violence.

Axios reported, citing sources, that if military operations resume against Iran, attacks would include widespread bombing of energy, infrastructure, and nuclear targets. An Israeli official said the likelihood of resuming operations before the US midterm elections is not high, but will increase significantly afterwards. Trump's national security team also discussed the matter, and Tehran-Washington negotiations have made no progress.

Shayan Samiei said that Donald Trump's contradictory messages about a possible attack on the Islamic Republic are part of Washington's effort to reduce the electoral costs of war. The US and Israel are acting cautiously but continue to pressure the Islamic Republic. Tehran may use proxy forces to change the equation, but any reckless action could have uncontrollable consequences.

Shahram Khaledi described Masoud Pezeshkian's trip to Turkmenistan as an effort to reduce the impact of the naval blockade. He said the capacity of Caspian Sea ports and rail routes is limited and cannot replace the main maritime routes. Additionally, Central Asian countries' relations with major powers limit Tehran's ability to bypass sanctions.

Channel 12 Israel reported that senior American officers informed Eyal Zamir that the White House and Pentagon have issued a readiness order for a large-scale attack on Iran. Zamir stated that such an operation could delay Israel's elections and face extensive missile retaliation from Tehran. Donald Trump has denied the possibility of an attack before the US elections.

Colonel Ali Rafiei, head of Tehran's public places police, spoke about young people in Sanai and Iranshahr streets who do not know why they come for walking. He also called for action against those who drive around these streets at night. This issue was discussed in a program hosted by Kambiz Hosseini.

Scott Bessent, US Treasury Secretary, said Washington is depriving Tehran's government of financial resources used for war in the region. The US Treasury Department imposed new sanctions under 'Operation Economic Exclusion' targeting Iran's shadow fleet. According to the department, most of the remaining network of this fleet has been effectively disabled.

The office of Prince Reza Pahlavi warned about the risk of executing Hadi Abbasian, a protester sentenced to death from Shirvan. Abbasian denied charges of ties to Israel and terrorism and was sentenced to death. Since his arrest, he has been denied family visits and access to a lawyer.

CNN reported that in Iran, individuals used OpenAI models and fake identities to publish critical content about the US war against Iran in American media. OpenAI stated that about 12 outlets published nearly 100 articles under seven fake journalists' names and has blocked accounts involved. It is unclear who is behind these activities and whether there is any connection to the Iranian government.

Penny Wong, Australia's foreign minister, expressed concern about the impact of attacks in Riyadh on oil prices and fuel costs in Australia. She called for a reduction in tensions and the continuation of negotiations between the US and Iran. Wong also emphasized the importance of reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

Nine Southeast Asian countries along with Japan and Australia emphasized developing oil reserves and creating regional shared reserves. ASEAN countries aim to increase the share of renewable energy to 30% of primary energy supply by 2030. An initial agreement was also reached to accelerate the implementation of the ASEAN power grid.

The Canadian Parliament hosted the Accountability Week for the Islamic Republic. Civil activists and Canadian party representatives presented a twelve-article plan to end judicial immunity for human rights violators in Iran. The event was held in cooperation with the Justice Collective for Iranians and the Raoul Wallenberg Human Rights Center.

Clashes between the Yemeni government army and the Houthis have intensified. The army spokesperson reported the destruction of hundreds of munitions and the killing of many Houthi forces. The Saudi-led coalition warned that Houthi attacks on civilians will not go unanswered.

Sadegh Beigdeli stated that war and negotiation between the Islamic Republic and the US occur simultaneously. He considered a stable agreement between the two countries unlikely. Any potential agreement would be short-term and unstable.

Miad Maleki stated that sanctions have always brought the Islamic Republic to the negotiating table. He added that sanctions on oil and petrochemical companies and pressure on exchange offices can increase economic pressure. These pressures push the Islamic Republic to negotiate to manage them.

OpenAI announced that nearly 100 articles were published in Iran using AI tools and fake identities. These articles, impersonating seven journalists, appeared in about 12 media outlets including Middle East Monitor. The content mainly criticized Washington's policies.

The Iran war has prompted Asian countries to strengthen their oil reserves and connect power grids. ASEAN member countries emphasized preparedness for energy crises in a meeting in Manila. Japan and Australia also supported strengthening regional oil reserves.

As the US midterm elections approach, the war with the Islamic Republic has become a political challenge for Donald Trump's administration. A possible shift in the balance of power in Congress could affect political and budgetary support for continuing the war. This issue was raised in a report by Golareh Han on Iran International.

Omid Memarian stated that the US demands concessions from Iran in the nuclear file. Tehran insists on releasing assets and lifting sanctions before fulfilling main commitments. The disagreement over the order of commitments has clouded the prospects for a meaningful agreement.

The match between Persepolis and Sanat Naft Abadan will be held on Friday, 17 Mehr 1405, at Ghal'eh Hasan Khan Stadium in Tehran. This game is part of the eighth week of the Premier League football. A poll about the match result is conducted on Iran International Sports Instagram page.

The Saudi Civil Aviation Authority announced that following two attacks on King Khalid International Airport, three citizens were killed and several injured. One of the Saudi airline's planes was damaged and one employee was killed. Airport operations returned to normal after the attacks.

The head of the Kurdistan judiciary announced the arrest of a suspect accused of sexual harassment in Divandarreh. The individual was arrested following complaints from five people and transferred to prison.

Malikeh Haghighat, a citizen of Gorgan, has been held in Gorgan prison for 80 days. Her legal case remains unresolved, and no court session has been held to address the charges against her. She faces accusations including propaganda against the regime.

A video recorded from a car shows that on the evening of October 8, an Iranian leopard was seen in the Asaluyeh road and the Golehdar–Shirino axis. The leopard was roaming at night. This sighting was recorded in a natural area.

The death sentences of three prisoners, including a woman, were carried out in Dezful and Sari prisons. These individuals had previously been sentenced to death for murder. The executions were carried out in separate cases.

Morteza Kazemian said Trump has given the Islamic Republic a deadline until the US midterm elections by maintaining the military option and continuing the economic blockade. He emphasized that the US and Israel ultimately seek to resolve the situation with the Islamic Republic. These statements were made on Iran International.

The prosecutor of Ilam announced the involvement of four medical staff members in the death of two pregnant women at Kosar Hospital. According to the forensic medical opinion, the attending physician, anesthesiologist, cardiologist, and nurse were negligent. This case is under investigation.

Vladimir Putin stated that Moscow is ready to do whatever it can to end the conflict. Masoud Pezeshkian said Tehran and Washington are reviewing new proposals to end the conflict. After finalizing the reforms, they plan to meet through mediators to reach an agreement.

The Norwegian Nobel Committee announced that Navanethem Pillay won the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for her efforts to promote peace and international law. She is an 85-year-old lawyer born in South Africa. This year, 287 candidates were registered for the prize.

The birthday ceremony of Mehrdad Yaghoubi Mehr was held on October 8 at his grave in Dorud, Lorestan. Mehrdad Yaghoubi Mehr was killed by agents on January 8, 2026, in the Ghal'eh Hassan Khan neighborhood of Tehran. He was 28 years old at the time of his death.

Hossein Aghaei from Iran International said that the interests of Russia and China in Ukraine and Taiwan could affect their approach towards the Islamic Republic. He emphasized that military, logistical, and intelligence support to the Islamic Republic might decrease. This could pressure Tehran to negotiate and accept more concessions.

Turki Al-Maliki, spokesperson for the coalition supporting Yemen's legitimate government, announced the destruction of three missile launch platforms belonging to the Houthis. These platforms were used to threaten regional security. He also emphasized that Houthi attacks on civilians will be firmly responded to.

The national Muay Thai selection competition in Qom with about 2,800 participants was canceled due to officials' objections to the female athletes' attire. The venue was filled with special forces and intelligence agents, and the women's competitions were completely canceled. Despite observing hijab, the athletes were criticized for their clothing and returned to their cities without competing.
Mehdi Saheli was killed on January 8th in public protests by direct gunfire from Khamenei's forces. His name remains in the memory of this land. His memory is a guiding light for freedom seekers.

The trial of three Iranians accused of cooperating with the Islamic Republic's intelligence service in the UK is ongoing. The prosecution stated they had surveilled two Iran International journalists for a violent attack. The accused took photos and videos of the journalists' residences and movements.

Niloufar Haghi Bozhani, a 22-year-old resident of Kermanshah, was arrested on Wednesday, October 7, by agents of the IRGC Intelligence Organization. The arrest was made without a judicial warrant at her family home. Her current location is unknown.

A citizen criticized the high price of red meat in a video sent to Iran International. He also expressed anger over the Islamic Republic's $200 million aid to Hezbollah. The citizen requested Prince Reza Pahlavi to return to Iran.

Reza Pahlavi stated on X social network that reforming the current structure is impossible and economic decline continues. He attributed the dollarization of the economy and the destruction of the national currency to instability, money printing, and corruption. He also described the nearly 90% inflation as a hidden tax benefiting those who print money.

The interrogation session of Asgar Akbarzadeh, a Turkic activist, was held at Branch 10 of the Public and Revolutionary Prosecutor's Office in Ardabil. He is accused of membership in an illegal group and propaganda against the regime and has defended himself. The session took place on October 5, 2026.

A citizen compared the value of Iranian currency to the euro in a video. He stated that the value of 2,468 Iranian rial coins is less than a 2-euro coin. This indicates a decrease in the value of Iranian currency.

A board member of the Trade Union Associations of East Azerbaijan criticized the current wages as insufficient to cover workers' real living costs. Many workers have resorted to overtime and second or third jobs to make up for income shortfalls. He emphasized that wages should be determined based on the real living basket and purchasing power of workers.

Marco Rubio criticized Amnesty International for its silence or inadequate response to the killing of protesters in Iran. This criticism reflects the concerns of Iranian citizens about the double standards of international organizations. Previously, political figures and human rights organizations had also highlighted this issue.

A 70-year-old woman was killed by her husband in the Majidieh neighborhood of Tehran. The suspect was arrested after confessing to the murder at the police station. This incident took place in Tehran.

Hassan Ameli, the Friday prayer leader of Ardabil, described the United Arab Emirates as the center of conspiracy against Arab and Islamic countries. He stated that the UAE is the fifth largest arms buyer in the world and that these weapons are sent to other countries to destabilize them. He also claimed that Israel is behind these conspiracies.

Nematollah Shahsavani and Alireza Farasti, two Iranian men accused of espionage in London, have denied the charges against them. They are accused of gathering information in July and August 2025. Their trial is scheduled for April next year.

The US Treasury Secretary announced that Washington will likely seize about one billion dollars of cryptocurrency assets linked to the Islamic Republic by the end of the week. This policy includes financial restrictions and blocking Iran's communication routes. The US is also working with the UAE and Oman and consulting with Pakistan and Turkey to close Iran's land entry and exit routes.

Yemeni government forces have gained full control of the Bab al-Mandab Strait and Mayun Island after a clearing operation. With air support from the coalition, they have secured positions overlooking this important shipping route. Dozens of Houthi fighters were killed and some surrendered during the clashes.

Three missile launch platforms used by the Houthis to attack Saudi Arabia have been destroyed. The Mecca Agreement can help train and equip Yemeni forces with the assistance of Turkey and Pakistan. It may take several weeks to months for these forces to reach optimal operational capability.

On the fourth anniversary of the deaths of Peyman Manbari, Yahya Rahimi, Dariush Alizadeh, and Mohammad Amini in the 2022 protests, families gathered at their graves in Sanandaj. The ceremony was held in their memory. The families commemorated them.

The trial of three Iranians accused of intelligence cooperation with the Islamic Republic in the UK has completed its first week. The prosecution has presented over 1,600 pieces of evidence including photos, videos, and exchanged messages. One of the accused used ChatGPT to find an address and surveillance methods.

The IRGC Navy announced that it targeted the LNG carrier "NV Sunshine" for illegal passage through the southern Strait of Hormuz. The ship suffered extensive fire damage. The IRGC warned that it controls the Strait of Hormuz and will not allow the presence of US military forces.

Taraneh and Romina Rahimi, two sisters arrested during the January 2026 protests, are held in Dolatabad Prison in Isfahan. Taraneh Rahimi has been sentenced to death and 11 years in prison, while Romina Rahimi received a 36-year sentence. Their lawyers have appealed these sentences to the Supreme Court.

Masoud Pezeshkian met with Vladimir Putin in Turkmenistan on October 8. The meeting took place on the sidelines of the Caspian Sea coastal countries and CIS leaders summits. Putin acknowledged Iran's efforts to end the conflict, and Pezeshkian emphasized continuing dialogue with the US despite attacks.

Scott Bessent, US Treasury Secretary, announced that Washington will likely confiscate about one billion dollars in cryptocurrency assets linked to the Islamic Republic by the end of the week. He said the Trump administration has turned the 'maximum pressure' campaign into a 'complete isolation' campaign. This policy includes financial restrictions and Iran's communication routes.

The New York Times and Wall Street Journal reported that the US government is considering new options for attacking Iran and strengthening its military presence in the Middle East. Donald Trump stated that the US will not attack Iran before the midterm elections. The Pentagon has prepared plans to strike Iran's military facilities, but Trump has rejected them.

OpenAI has blocked accounts linked to an Iranian media infiltration operation. Nearly 100 articles about the Iran-US war were published using ChatGPT and fake journalist identities. These articles were posted or reposted on about 12 online media outlets in different countries.

An independent international organization reported that the Islamic Republic is moving towards an illegal economy to counter US sanctions. This report was released amid the intensification of the Trump administration's economic isolation campaign. An interview was conducted with Ahmad Samadi, a journalist from Iran International.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations reported that a ship 13 nautical miles west of Algiers in the UAE was hit by an unknown projectile and caught fire. The fire has been controlled, but the crew's condition and damage extent are still unknown. Authorities are investigating the incident and have urged passing ships to exercise caution.

An initial agreement has been made to allocate over 110 hectares of land in Chabahar to Afghanistan. Mohsen Zangeneh stated that the land will be provided to Afghanistan for investment. Social media users have raised questions about the details and fate of this land.

The 2026 Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to Navi Pillay, a South African human rights activist. UN officials welcomed the award as a sign of the importance of international justice. This has sparked many reactions among international officials and countries.

Ahmad Alamolhoda, the Friday prayer leader of Mashhad, said the enemy aims to create rivals for popular gatherings by organizing vulgar programs in various cities. He added that some officials support this secular front as joy and vitality, which actually belongs to the enemy. Alamolhoda emphasized that revolutionary people do not participate in these programs and the enemy's goal is to reduce people's resistance.

A video shows a cleric and a supporter of mandatory hijab arguing with a woman in a park in Qom about compulsory dress code. The woman responded that arguing with them is like teaching integrals to a fish in the sea. This video was released by Iran International.

Omid Ghanooni, a 17-year-old from Arjenk, Khansar, died after being arrested and beaten. His family protested in front of the Vist police station demanding accountability. His funeral was held with a large public attendance.

Amid the intensification of the Trump administration's economic isolation campaign, the Global Initiative against Transnational Organized Crime has reported that the Islamic Republic is moving towards expanding illegal economic activities to counter the pressure of US sanctions.

A citizen explained in a video to Iran International that the prices of some fruits and vegetables fluctuate. He claims that a mafia is manipulating the prices. According to him, the economic situation will not improve.

UN human rights experts stated that security forces of the Islamic Republic killed thousands of protesters in the December 2025 protests. They emphasized that none of the detainees from these protests should be executed. The UN independent fact-finding mission has classified the killing of protesters as a crime against humanity.

The Saudi ambassador announced that the Bab al-Mandab Strait has been cleared of Houthi presence. Pro-government Yemeni forces have advanced in the area with Saudi air support. So far, there is no sign of ground troops from Turkey or Pakistan being sent to fight the Houthis.

A Lebanese media network reported that details of the $200 million financial aid from the Islamic Republic to Hezbollah will soon be announced in a press conference. The head of Hezbollah's executive council will explain how the funds will be distributed. Reuters had previously reported that the aid was given for distribution among war victims.

A roadside bomb exploded near a police vehicle in the Cheshmeh Ziarat area of Zahedan. Nosrat Eftekhari, the social deputy of the police in Sistan and Baluchestan province, was killed in the incident. The main perpetrator was killed while fleeing, and several police officers were injured.

A video shows Amirali Heidari's uncle crying beside his grave. Amirali Heidari, 17 years old, was killed by security forces during the protests on January 8, 2026, in Kermanshah. This incident has been shared on social media.

On the occasion of the International Day Against the Death Penalty, a one-year report on executions in Iran has been published. This report was provided by HRANA news agency. Contact information and HRANA channel details are also mentioned.

Human rights activists called for an immediate halt to executions in Iran on the International Day Against the Death Penalty. They documented 2,003 executions in the past year, including 69 political cases, and criticized the systematic use of executions for political repression. They also demanded replacing death sentences with other punishments and ending torture and forced confessions.

Hashem Hosseini Bushehri, the Friday prayer leader of Qom, said in his sermon that laxity in some cities breaks the hearts of believers and makes streets unsafe. He described these individuals as frontline soldiers of the enemies and warned that the enemies seek a cultural assault leading to nudity in society. He emphasized that the enemies have other plans and the nation must remain resilient.
A citizen reported that they refueled at a gas station but the banking system is down. They cannot pay with any bank card. This issue occurred during fuel payment.

Scott Bessent, the US Treasury Secretary, announced that the UAE and Oman are cooperating in the "complete isolation" campaign against Iran. The US is also consulting with Pakistan and Turkey to close land routes to and from Iran. This campaign includes financial, maritime, air, and land restrictions.

Mostafa Mirsalim stated that car imports benefit the exporting country and that traffic fatalities are due to poor driving, not the quality of domestic cars. He considered importing foreign cars as an obstacle to the country's progress. He also called accusations against the quality of domestic cars baseless.

Iran International's audience reports the presence of government forces and special units in public places and schools in Tehran. The security atmosphere in Iranian cities has intensified. This report is based on an interview with Saba Heydarkhani.

The Yemeni Foreign Ministry called on the UN Security Council to take decisive action following Houthi attacks on King Khalid Airport and a Saudi airplane. These attacks resulted in three deaths and several injuries. Yemen considers Iran's support for the Houthis as the cause of the continuation of these attacks.

In Zanjan province, the commander of the Basij base of the Cultural Heritage Department and a municipality employee were involved in suppressing and killing protesters. Five out of eight counties in the province joined the popular protests. Iran International has covered the geography of the national revolution in Zanjan.

UN human rights experts have called for an immediate halt to executions in Iran. The statement highlights violations of fair trial rights and the use of executions to instill fear. Hasan Naib-Hashem described these issues as violations of defendants' rights.

The Friday prayer leader of Ahvaz stated that the Iranian nation will not retreat from its right to enrichment or from the Strait of Hormuz. He emphasized that the will of the Iranian nation is above the will of global arrogance. He also commented that Trump has psychological disorders and tells many lies.

The mother of Atefeh Abed placed nine apples in a container on the ninth month after her daughter's death and spoke about the injustice done to her. Atefeh Abed, 23 years old, was killed by direct gunfire from government forces in Mashhad. This video was recently released.

Mirsalim stated that gasoline in Iran is free and priced at 1500 tomans. He acknowledged that Iranian cars are of lower quality compared to foreign cars and mentioned the lack of economic justification for fuel consumption reduction projects. The program host disagreed, citing people's income levels.

A citizen sent a video showing the eternal graves in the city of Alvand. He says the eternal ones are not anonymous. A relative of Shahabeddin Mousavi said they did not allow him to be buried in his own city.

Sanat Naft Abadan fans demanded the dismissal of Mohammad Nouri after their fourth loss this season. Nouri mentioned some players' carelessness in a press conference and had offered his resignation in week seven, which was not accepted. The team has not won any matches in 8 weeks and is at the bottom of the league with 4 points.

Reports indicate shortages of essential medicines such as insulin and fluoxetine in pharmacies. The cost of blood pressure and heart medications has significantly increased. Economic problems including unemployment, poverty, and rising prices of work tools have been reported in various cities.

Human rights activists in Iran reported that 2,003 people were executed in the past year. At least 69 of those executed faced political and security charges. The organization has called for an immediate halt to executions.
